hook_gate_detail: Assigned #2 Listicle/Number; script hook_type=2; previous episode (2026-11-18-gta6-sick-day) used #1. Opener 'Three money mistakes on G T A six launch day.' promises 3 and pays all 3 (Ultimate, pay later, cheap key) in order. Passes. Weakness: opener is a bare title-like statement, no picture/tension beyond the number.

ok: $20/twenty dollars, 25%/twenty-five percent, 47%/forty-seven percent, 3 mistakes/Three all match across say/text/visual/on_screen/upload
findings: Line 1: text 'G T A 6' vs say 'G T A six' is acceptable per Rule B convention, but scene 1 shows a store sign 'GTA 6' (written form allowed on signs, only if not read as a caption). Keep it off captions.
Line 7: on_screen 'DOZENS FAKE SITES' vs visual headline 'DOZENS OF FAKE SITES' differ; pick one, make it match 'dozens of fake sites'.
Line 8: say/text 'keep the twenty' (idiom, no unit) vs screen '+$20' and upload '$20'; say 'twenty dollars' so voice = screen.
Line 5: voice 'users paid late' omits 'pay later' but on-screen is '47% PAID LATE'; screen has no 'of pay-later users', so the population is ambiguous (see fix).
NordVPN: TTS may mispronounce 'NordVPN' (non-native/Kokoro); caption 'NordVPN' vs heard form could differ. Verify audio or write 'Nord V P N' in both.

extra_checks.story_vs_narrator: Mostly narrator reading a list: 'First/Second/Third, Benny buys...' in third person, Benny never speaks, no you-address. Visual gags exist (wallet coughs, bills rain, bugs bury him) so sound-off entertainment is decent, but the voice track is a list read-out. No twist beyond item 3.
extra_checks.nord_hedged: Mostly. 'dozens' only, no invented victims or losses, and matches the research. But the source says dozens of sites for fake pre-orders, beta access and phishing for Social Club logins, not all malware; 'fake sites that spread malware' narrows it. Also a 'cheap key' is not what the source describes (fake pre-orders/early access). Say 'fake pre-order sites' or 'fake sites, some with malware'.
extra_checks.bnpl_47: Does not say people finance GTA 6, but 'of users' is ambiguous right after 'he uses pay later', and scene 4 shows Benny paying later (implicitly for the game). Say 'of pay later users' and keep scene 4 from showing a game purchase on credit.
extra_checks.do_not_claim: No Rockstar art, no Ultimate item names, no loss totals, no guaranteed income, no 'people buy games with BNPL' line. 'NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE' present. Nothing forbidden claimed.
extra_checks.upload: Good: title pays off, line 1 'Number three could wreck your computer, not just your wallet.' is a real hook, 4 hashtags, 'Not financial advice.' present. Note the voice never teases number three; that tease only lives in the description.

fixes: Line 1 (hook, 7): add tension, e.g. 'Three money mistakes Benny makes on G T A six launch day. Number three is the worst.' (keep <=12 words per sentence). That also plants the open loop (6).
Whole script (stakes 6): never addresses the viewer. Add a 'you' line, e.g. line 3 'That is twenty dollars of your money, or twenty-five percent, more.' or line 5 'Maybe you do this too.'
Line 4/5 (surprise 7, clarity 7): say 'LendingTree found forty-seven percent of pay later users paid late.' It fixes the BNPL population and avoids implying game financing.
Line 7: change to 'NordVPN found dozens of fake game sites. Some spread malware.' and fix on_screen/headline mismatch; confirm TTS says NordVPN clearly.
Line 8 (ending 8, clarity 7): 'keep the twenty' -> 'keep the twenty dollars'; the voice also should state the lesson (e.g. pay in full, official store) before the A/B, so the payoff >= the promise.

Entertainment 6: let Benny react aloud or add a gag per item (e.g. Benny's I-saved-twenty smirk breaks when the bill arrives); items 1 and 2 have no real consequence beat, only item 3 pays off with action.
Open loop/escalation: items 1 and 2 are flat declarative (First/Second/Third pattern). Vary phrasing and add the 'number three' tease to the voice.
